run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Root-cause investigation of the failing signup service in namespace app-162, following the approved runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook. Step 1 (signup pods/status/logs): both signup-service pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-6xjkz, signup-service-7c89545dc9-n26sj) are phase Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False / ContainersNotReady, and their logs repeat `ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>` with `GET /ready HTTP/1.1 503` every 5 s — so readiness, and therefore Service registration, fails on the payments dependency. Step 2 (payments health): payments-service-6d94c44fdc-npkjt is also Running-but-not-Ready with restartCount 0, and its own log states `STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail` and `Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key`, with `/health` and `/ready` returning 503. Step 3 (service-to-service path): the Endpoints object app-162/payments-service contains only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.45), which is consistent with the connection-refused errors seen by signup; no networkpolicy is present in the returned set. Step 4 (payments-specific checks): the Stripe authentication failure is directly evidenced; no database error line was observed in the startup log lines read. Step 5 (env): pod spec shows STRIPE_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL sourced only from secretKeyRef (payments-secrets/stripe-api-key and payments-secrets/database-url; signup uses signup-secrets/database-url) — secrets cannot be read, so the actual values were not verified. The observed fault is a bad Stripe credential in the payments dependency, which makes payments unready, has no ready endpoints, and causes signup's /ready to fail so users cannot register. Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every call, so error-rate, latency and trace evidence for app-162 is unknown, not zero; the conclusion rests on Kubernetes object state, endpoints and container logs, hence partial.

claims.text: In namespace app-162, both signup-service pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-6xjkz and signup-service-7c89545dc9-n26sj) are phase Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady and message "containers with unready status: [signup-service]"; no waiting reason and no last termination state are recorded.

Signup pod logs show the application failing its readiness work because of the payments dependency: signup-service-7c89545dc9-6xjkz logs `2026-11-22 09:38:25/30/35/40 - ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>` each followed by `GET /ready HTTP/1.1 503`, and signup-service-7c89545dc9-n26sj shows the same pattern.

payments-service-6d94c44fdc-npkjt is phase Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False (ContainersNotReady, "containers with unready status: [payments-service]"), state running started 2026-11-22T09:38:20Z, and empty lastState.

The payments-service container log states `2026-11-22 09:38:22,283 - ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail` and repeatedly `ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key`, while probe requests `GET /ready` and `GET /health` return 503 at 09:38:25-09:38:40.

Deployment payments-service reports Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ("Deployment does not have minimum availability."), unavailableReplicas 1 of replicas 1; Deployment signup-service reports the same condition with unavailableReplicas 2 of replicas 2.

Endpoints object app-162/payments-service holds only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.45, targetRef Pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-npkjt) on port 8080, i.e. the payments Service had no ready endpoint; Endpoints app-162/signup-service likewise lists only notReadyAddresses for both signup pods. This matches the signup-side connection-refused errors against http://payments-service:8080.

The payments-service Deployment container gets STRIPE_API_KEY only from secretKeyRef name payments-secrets key stripe-api-key and DATABASE_URL from payments-secrets key database-url; the signup-service template sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080 and takes DATABASE_URL from signup-secrets key database-url. The secret values themselves could not be read.

Both app-162 Deployments are generation 1 / deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, created 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z, and the only ReplicaSets in the namespace are signup-service-7c89545dc9 and payments-service-6d94c44fdc (created 09:38:19Z, no template annotations such as restartedAt), so no older ReplicaSet or template-unchanged restart sequence is visible for these workloads.

Cluster events in the window for app-162 contain only Normal lifecycle records: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (payments-service 0->1, signup-service 0->2), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, plus two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint entries for Endpoints/app-162/signup-service ("endpoints \"signup-service\" already exists") and Endpoints/app-95/orca; no Pod Unhealthy, Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff events appear (5 events outside the window were dropped).

The flagd demo flags (ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, demo.flagd.json) that could inject payment faults — paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable — are state ENABLED but with defaultVariant "off", as are all other listed flags; these flags belong to the otel-demo demo applications, a different set of workloads from app-162/payments-service.

The otel-demo namespace workloads I checked at pod level were Ready: all 22 pods are phase Running with ready=true, including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and frontend/checkout/cart; the only lastState anomalies are kube-state-metrics (lastState Error, exit 2) and prometheus-readonly-proxy (lastState Error, exit 1), which are monitoring components in a different namespace from the failing signup workload.

Payments-service is not crashlooping: restartCount 0, no lastState termination, no waiting reason and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff event; the container reached state running and answers probes with 503 rather than failing to start.

Fault-injection feature flag in the demo flagd config as the cause of the app-162 signup/payments failure was rejected: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are at defaultVariant "off", and those flags govern the otel-demo demo workloads, not the app-162 python services.

The proximate cause of signup's readiness failure is the readiness of payments-service: because payments-service had no ready endpoint (only notReadyAddresses), signup's HTTP call to http://payments-service:8080 is refused at the network level, so signup's /ready returns 503 and Kubernetes keeps both signup pods out of the Service.

The deepest evidenced cause is the Stripe credential value in use by payments-service: the application itself reports that STRIPE_API_KEY is set to an invalid test key, and that key is supplied only through secretKeyRef app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key. Whether the secret holds a stale/placeholder value or an intended test key, and when it changed, could not be verified because Secret contents are not readable.

A second candidate not yet excluded is a problem in the signup service's own DATABASE_URL (secret app-162/signup-secrets key database-url): the logs read cover only the startup window in which /ready aborted on the payments check first, so database connectivity was never exercised in the observed lines. No database error line was observed, but its absence in 9-14 startup lines does not prove the database is fine.

Check and correct the Stripe credential held by Secret app-162/payments-secrets under key stripe-api-key (the value is unreadable through these tools, so verify it out-of-band against a valid key), then let the payments-service pod become ready and confirm its /health and /ready stop returning 503 before expecting signup to register users.

Runbook steps that still need carrying out once tooling allows: directly test service-to-service reachability (runbook step 3, e.g. curl http://payments-service:8080/health from a signup pod and port-forward the payments Service) and inspect the payments container environment (runbook step 5) — no exec/port-forward capability was available in this Run, and the pod-spec secretKeyRef was checked instead.

gaps: Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every call (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target) and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services, traces_search), so no error-rate, latency, transaction or trace evidence exists for app-162/signup-service or app-162/payments-service; those signals are unknown, not zero.

Secret app-162/payments-secrets (keys stripe-api-key, database-url) and Secret app-162/signup-secrets could not be read, so the actual STRIPE_API_KEY value, when it was changed, and the validity of the signup database URL were not verified; change history is also a not_integrated source.

The queries for networkpolicies, resourcequotas in app-162 and for ConfigMap data containing STRIPE/invalid/signup/payments returned no_data, so a policy- or quota-based cause is unchecked rather than excluded; the ConfigMap listing across all namespaces returned only 21 ConfigMaps with unrelated keys (kube-root-ca.crt, otel-demo demo/flagd/prometheus content).

Container logs cover only 2026-11-22T09:38:22Z onward (pods created 09:38:19Z, no previous container instance existed), so what happened earlier in the 24-hour authorized window is unknown; events are limited to 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z-09:38:20Z with 5 events outside the window dropped.

No root-cause change record was found for the invalid Stripe credential: no object applying a fault to payments-service was observed, and the deployment is generation 1/revision 1, so whether the secret was wrong from creation or changed later is unresolved.

User-visible registration failure is inferred from signup pods being excluded from Endpoints and /ready returning 503; no direct /register request log or trace was available to confirm customer impact.

The two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events (Endpoints signup-service "already exists" in app-162, and Endpoints app-95/orca) name objects in a namespace app-95 that no longer exists in the namespace list; their relevance to this failure is unverified.
next_steps: Verify the STRIPE_API_KEY value stored in Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) out-of-band and replace it with a valid key if it is the placeholder test value.

After correcting the credential, confirm payments-service becomes Ready (kubectl get pods -l app=payments-service) and that /health and /ready return 200, then confirm both signup-service pods become Ready and the app-162/signup-service Endpoints gain ready addresses.

Exercise an actual registration request through the signup Service once endpoints are ready, and add a temporary check that signup's dependency on payments cannot block its own readiness (or make the payments check non-fatal) so registrations are not blocked by a third-party credential.
Re-check error rate, latency and traces for signup-service and payments-service once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, to quantify the failure window and confirm recovery.

Confirm whether app-162/payments-service and app-162/signup-service are expected to run in this cluster at all (they were created at 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z, replicas scaled from 0), and, if this is a test fixture, whether an invalid Stripe key is intentionally provisioned.
